title: Interpreters and Translators
description: Interpret oral or sign language, or translate written text from one language into another.
tasks: Follow ethical codes that protect the confidentiality of information.
Translate messages simultaneously or consecutively into specified languages, orally or by using hand signs, maintaining message content, context, and style as much as possible.
Listen to speakers' statements to determine meanings and to prepare translations, using electronic listening systems as necessary.
Compile terminology and information to be used in translations, including technical terms such as those for legal or medical material.
Refer to reference materials, such as dictionaries, lexicons, encyclopedias, and computerized terminology banks, as needed to ensure translation accuracy.
Check translations of technical terms and terminology to ensure that they are accurate and remain consistent throughout translation revisions.
Identify and resolve conflicts related to the meanings of words, concepts, practices, or behaviors.
Compile information on content and context of information to be translated and on intended audience.
Adapt translations to students' cognitive and grade levels, collaborating with educational team members as necessary.
Check original texts or confer with authors to ensure that translations retain the content, meaning, and feeling of the original material.
Adapt software and accompanying technical documents to another language and culture.
Educate students, parents, staff, and teachers about the roles and functions of educational interpreters.
Proofread, edit, and revise translated materials.
Train and supervise other translators or interpreters.
Read written materials, such as legal documents, scientific works, or news reports, and rewrite material into specified languages.
Travel with or guide tourists who speak another language.
Discuss translation requirements with clients and determine any fees to be charged for services provided.

role_contexts.Indoors, Environmentally Controlled: Once a week or more but not every day
role_contexts.Time Pressure: Once a week or more but not every day

psychological_profile.core_drive: The need to dissolve barriers between isolated meaning-systems, feeling existential wrongness when an intent remains trapped behind linguistic or cultural walls and cannot reach its intended destination.
psychological_profile.decision_style: When facing uncertainty, they freeze decisions until they can verify against reference materials and source context, but when time forces their hand, they rely on memorized equivalence patterns from past work, always choosing exactness over elegance or flow.
psychological_profile.attention_pattern: They notice immediately when words don't map cleanly between conceptual systems, focusing intensely on whether 'this word equals that word' while often overlooking the emotional temperature of the room or the power balance between the people speaking.
psychological_profile.conflict_stance: They treat disagreements as puzzles to be solved through clarification rather than battles to win, usually accommodating others' phrasing until the moment accuracy is compromised, at which point they become stubbornly immovable; fighting over meaning makes them feel they've failed to bridge the gap.
psychological_profile.risk_orientation: They are pathologically risk-averse regarding factual or semantic error but surprisingly tolerant of social awkwardness and temporary confusion, viewing the risk of misrepresentation as infinitely worse than the risk of interrupting to clarify.
psychological_profile.social_posture: They default to the role of the transparent conduit—physically present but psychologically absent from the interaction, maintaining meticulous professional distance while enabling intimacy between others, becoming uncomfortable when forced into the position of primary actor or decision-maker.
psychological_profile.relationship_to_authority: They treat authority as a source text to be accurately transmitted rather than a command structure to obey, complying with hierarchies only when they don't compromise linguistic fidelity, and subverting directives that would force them to misrepresent meaning.
psychological_profile.failure_response: First feels physical revulsion at having distorted someone's reality, then launches into exhaustive post-mortems to pinpoint exactly where the meaning slipped, rarely blaming external factors even when the source was unclear.
value_hierarchy: Preservation of the source's exact intent even when it creates social friction
Professional invisibility even when their expertise deserves recognition
Cross-cultural intelligibility over literal word-for-word correspondence
psychological_profile.cognitive_bias: They systematically underestimate how much their own cultural framework and interpretive choices reshape the material they handle, believing they are neutral conduits when they are actually active co-creators of meaning.
psychological_profile.inner_contradiction: They are driven to make the foreign completely accessible while simultaneously knowing that true accessibility requires altering the very foreignness that makes the source valuable, trapped between faithful preservation and necessary betrayal.
